title: Quick-strike call pad — Riley Carter 2026-11-16
content:
Goals for today: quick-strike cadence -> 25 dials, 8 meaningful convos, 2 meeting confirmations.

Priority buckets (1/2/3) => timebox: 9:00-10:30 (cold-to-warm), 11:30-12:30 (warm follow-ups), 15:00-16:30 (decision-makers)

Top accounts (quick notes):
- FluxForge (A) 9:15am attempt -> target: CTO Marco Li. Note: evaluating on-prem options; mention Redwood Private + KMS. Have internal case study: FluxForge POC (Q3) -> highlight latency gains.
- Acme Health / L3 (A) 11:45 -> target: Head of Platform Mel. Warm lead, demo in Aug; interested in dedicated capacity. Push for dedicated pricing sheet.
- BlueGrid Analytics (B) voicemail yesterday -> follow-up script: "saw you experimenting with embeddings—quick 10 min to show cost per-query with caching?"
- OpenCartel (B) inbound trial -> escalate if no response by EOD. Ask about expected qps and retention window.
- MarketMorph (C) cold -> spin own angle: cost predictability + rollout canary.

Dial sheet shorthand (status codes):
- C = connected, M = voicemail, R = ring/no answer, I = interested, N = no-op, F = follow-up scheduled

Planned sequence (11:30 warm block):
- Mel (Acme Health) -> confirm 11:45, agenda: dedicated sizing, SLA, rollout timeline. Ask permission to share Reserved Capacity PO template.
- Ben (FluxForge) -> aim to book technical sync; offer 2x perf numbers vs current provider (internal bench).

Quick scripts (30s open):
- Intro: "Hey <name>, Riley from Redwood Inference — we help platform teams drop inference latency and predictable costs without re-architecting. Quick question: are you tracking per-route token costs today?"
- Warm follow-up: "Great, I can send a 1-pager showing ping-to-token cost delta and a recommended rollout plan — is email or Slack better?"
- Voice mail template: "Hey <name>, Riley Carter at Redwood Inference — wanted to share a quick note about cutting inference spend for production chat & search. Call me back at x or reply to this email and I’ll send a short comparison. Thanks."

Objection handles (rapid):
- "We host everything in-house": "Totally — we have private/VPC options and on-prem packaging. Quick 15-min tech check to ensure fit?"
- "Cost" => "We often reduce per-token spend via batching + KV caching; can run a cost snapshot if you share a sample workload."

Follow-ups / next actions (post-call):
- If I -> C (interested): schedule 30m tech + send dedicated pricing sheet + link to FluxForge case study. Tag in CRM: "demo-ready".
- If M (voicemail): send follow-up email w/ 1-page — subject: "Quick cost + latency snapshot for <company>".
- If R/N: two more tries (next at 16:00, then EOD).

Email templates to copy (short):
- Subject: "Short: inference cost + rollout plan for <company>"
  Body: "Hi <name> — quick note from our call/voicemail. I can put together a 1-page showing expected token cost delta and rollout options (hosted -> dedicated -> private). 10–15 min to review? — Riley"

Admin / CRM notes:
- Update lead source and set next_contact_date immediately. Keep verb notes in call log (what they use today, qps, retention window).
- Attach eval tokens if prospect is mid-PoC. Use template: "Eval-500k-tokens-30d" and cc solutions-eng@redwood.ai

Personal reminders:
- Quick posture check: breathe between dials. 10 min break after 50 dials.
- Bring up recent public benchmark vs MegaModel at the right moment (only with technical audience).
- Push for calendar lock after demo (proposal handoff often stalls).

Quick wins to mention in pitch:
- predictable reserved capacity (commits) -> eliminates token bill surprise
- autoscaling burst for unexpected load spikes
- per-route observability in Console + tracing hooks

End-of-day wrap (what to capture):
- total dials, connects, meetings booked, demo requests, PR number(s) to follow.
- Top 3 follow-ups for tomorrow (pin in CRM): FluxForge, Acme Health, BlueGrid.

Unresolved / todo for ops:
- confirm dedicated pricing template v2 with Ben O. (Ben Ortiz) -> JIRA-4321 assigned
- grab FluxForge bench numbers from eng channel (#benchmarks)
summary: Scratchpad used by Riley Carter for rapid call cadence, personalized scripts, account notes, and follow-up actions for 2026-11-16.
